Meta.Documentation:
The substitution process has to directions: 1. Xyna data type writing to JSON (data type -> JSON) 2. JSON parsed to Xyna Data Type (JSON -> data type)
Depending on these directions, the following member variables have to be set: 1. Data type -> JSON The json key specified by "pathToMemberInDataType" in the data type will be substituted by "jsonName" in the JSON document.
Example: - pathToMemberInDataType=info.a - jsonName=@a!
=> transforms info a: 1 b: 2
into "info" : {"@a!" : "1", "b" : 2}
2. JSON -> data type The json key specified by "pathToMemberInDataType" in the JSON document will be substituted by "jsonName" in the data type.
Example: - pathToMemberInDataType=@a! - jsonName=info.a
=> transforms "info" : {"@a!" : "1", "b" : 2}
into info a: 1 b: 2
Note: If a complex substructure has to be substituted, where the parent was already substituded as well, the parent paths or JSON names have to be specified with the new replacement. This is needed regardless of the direction.

Data.Label: Path to Member in Data Type

Meta.Documentation:
Case 1 - data type -> JSON: Path given by member var names (not labels!), separated by dots. If member var name is a list, then append "[]", except if path ends with the list.
Example: router.interfaces vs router.interfaces[].supportedtypes
Case 2 - JSON -> data type: JSON name in the document, which has to be substituted.
